眠.meaning: Every <part>eye</part> in the village starts to droop. The <part>people</part> yawn in the square, lids sliding shut one by one, until the whole town is snoring on the cobbles. Nobody stirs until noon: they all <kanji>sleep</kanji>.
眠.on: A <sound>mean</sound> rooster stomps through the square crowing at them, but they just roll over and keep snoring.
眠.kun: The only bed left is a fishing <sound>ne</sound>t, so a <sound>moo</sound>se curls up in it and dozes off too.

夏.meaning: Under <part>one</part> flat, blazing sky, a man drags his <part>folding chair</part> up to a <part>phone booth</part> just to sit in its thin strip of shade. Sweat drips, ice cream melts, the road goes soft. It's the height of <kanji>summer</kanji>.
夏.on: Inside the booth someone has left a bucket with a gasping <sound>ca</sound>rp, longing for a cool pond.
夏.kun: He cracks open a bag of salted <sound>nuts</sound> and munches them in the shade, still sweating.

法.meaning: Grandma dries the dishes her own way: she flicks off the <part>water drops</part>, waves her hand, and they're <part>gone</part>, every time, in the same three steps. Nobody else can do it. It's her secret <kanji>method</kanji>.
法.on: Her way of washing them is just as odd: a blast from the garden <sound>ho</sound>se, straight through the kitchen window.
法.kun: '<sound>No</sound>, not like that!' she snaps when you try, and points you to a pile of plates as big as a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

耳.meaning: A tall frame with two bars inside and a long base that sticks out at the bottom, curled like the folds on the side of your head. Whisper into it and it twitches: it heard every word. It's an <kanji>ear</kanji>.
耳.on: A muddy <sound>jee</sound>p roars past so loudly that you clap both hands over your ears.
耳.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat perches by your left ear and another <sound>mee</sound>rkat by your right, both listening for danger.

取.meaning: A seagull swoops down, snatches the <part>pretzel</part> right out of your hand and gives your <part>ear</part> a tug on its way back up. It doesn't ask and it doesn't share. It just likes to <kanji>take</kanji>.
取.on: Up on the roof it dips your pretzel in a bag of <sound>su</sound>gar it took from someone else.
取.kun: Then it flies off with its prize to the top of a <sound>to</sound>tem pole, where nobody can reach it.

撮.meaning: A photographer ties her boot to an <part>anchor</part> and climbs to the <part>utmost</part> tip of the ship's mast, leaning out as far as she dares into the storm. Click! One perfect <kanji>snapshot</kanji>.
撮.on: In the photo, a single <sound>satsu</sound>ma rolls across the grey deck, bright orange against the waves.
撮.kun: Her next shot is a <sound>to</sound>tem pole on the shore, waving past as the ship sails by.

黄.meaning: A painter scratches a <part>hash sign</part> on the lid of a jar, stands it on two legs shaped like an <part>eight</part>, and fills it with sunshine. Ask her the <part>reason</part> and she just grins: every drop inside is <kanji>yellow</kanji>.
黄.on: She dips her brush in it and paints a huge <sound>oa</sound>k, every leaf bright yellow.
黄.kun: The lid of the jar only opens with a tiny yellow <sound>key</sound>.

横.meaning: A <part>tree</part> grows beside a tall <part>yellow</part> wall that blocks out the sun. So it gives up on going upward and grows flat out to one side, its branches stretching along the ground like a fence. It never goes up, only <kanji>sideways</kanji>.
横.on: In the end it's a proud old <sound>oa</sound>k lying on its side, and squirrels use it as a bridge.
横.kun: A pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt slides sideways off a branch and lands on a sleeping <sound>ko</sound>ala.

断.meaning: A sack of <part>rice</part> hangs from a <part>pole</part>, held up by <part>one</part> rope along the bottom. Swing! An <part>axe</part> slices through the rope, the sack thumps down and the grains spill free. A clean cut: <kanji>severance</kanji>.
断.on: The sack falls straight through a trapdoor into a dripping <sound>dun</sound>geon below.
断.kun: The axe comes down so hard it also chops a bath <sound>tu</sound>b clean in two.

成.meaning: You throw a <part>boomerang</part> at a <part>spear</part> stuck in the ground. It wraps round the shaft, the two fuse together, and with a puff of smoke they <kanji>turn into</kanji> a brand-new tool: a long hook on a stick.
成.on: The new tool is perfect for one job: hooking open a locked steel <sound>sa</sound>fe.
成.kun: Inside the safe is a puffy <sound>na</sound>an, which turns into a pillow the moment you touch it.

嫌.meaning: A <part>woman</part> is told to do two chores <part>concurrently</part>: rake the lawn and hold two posts upright, both at once. She drops the lot, folds her arms and scowls. She doesn't hate much, but this she really does <kanji>dislike</kanji>.
嫌.on: She'd rather scrub out the dog <sound>ken</sound>nel, and she hates that too.
嫌.kun: '<sound>Ee</sound>k!' she shrieks, as the dog drags a soggy ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn out of the kennel.

財.meaning: A <part>genius</part> works out that <part>shellfish</part> shells make great coins. He collects them, polishes them and stacks them to the ceiling. His house, his boat, his hat: he bought it all with shells. Look at all his <kanji>property</kanji>.
財.on: His proudest buy is a <sound>xy</sound>lophone with keys made of shells, which he plays to count his money.
財.kun: He keeps the best shells in a bath <sound>tu</sound>b guarded by a <sound>ca</sound>rp, and cheers '<sound>Rah</sound>!' each time he adds one.

刺.meaning: You reach into a <part>thorn bush</part> for a berry, and something jabs you like a tiny <part>dagger</part>. Ouch! You pull your finger out, and there it is, stuck in your skin: a <kanji>thorn</kanji>.
刺.on: Next time you go berry picking, you hold a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld out in front of you.
刺.kun: To cheer you up, a friend brings you a grilled <sound>sa</sound>rdine stabbed on a stick.

焼.meaning: A <part>fire</part> roars in the oven, and smoke curls out of the <part>chimney</part> above it. The whole street smells of warm bread and cinnamon. Someone in there is about to <kanji>bake</kanji> the best loaf in town.
焼.on: The baker turns it into a cooking <sound>show</sound>, and a crowd presses against the window to watch the loaves rise.
焼.kun: A cat curls up by the warm oven with a ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn, and its fur gets a little toasted.

坊.meaning: On a heap of <part>soil</part> in the backyard, someone has stuck up a stick with a hanky for a <part>sail</part>, and he is steering his mud ship across the seven seas. Muddy knees, big grin, wooden sword: it's a little <kanji>boy</kanji>.
坊.on: His mud ship crashes into a giant <sound>bou</sound>lder, and he plants his flag on it and calls it an island.

荷.meaning: A traveller staggers through tall <part>grass</part> with a bundle on his back so huge that people stop and stare. '<part>What</part> on earth is in there?' they ask. He only shrugs and keeps walking under his <kanji>baggage</kanji>.
荷.on: Something wriggles inside: a live <sound>ca</sound>rp, flipping about in a bucket of water.
荷.kun: The bundle bursts at one seam, so he stitches it shut with a sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle, right there in the grass.

遠.meaning: A princess in a trailing <part>ball gown</part> walks up a <part>ramp</part> that never seems to end. She climbs and climbs, her train sweeping behind her, and the palace at the top is still just a dot on the horizon. It's so <kanji>distant</kanji>.
遠.on: Halfway up she hears the hum of an <sound>en</sound>gine: a little cart has come to offer her a ride.
遠.kun: Her slippers wear through, and she stubs her big <sound>toe</sound> on every step of the long, long way.

骨.meaning: In the museum, a <part>frame</part> holds up an old <part>blanket</part>, and under it, lit by the <part>moon</part> through the skylight, something rattles. Lift the blanket: bones, bones and more bones. It's a whole <kanji>skeleton</kanji>.
骨.on: A <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs onto its ribs, and the dust makes it sneeze: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!'
骨.kun: A guard drops his <sound>ho</sound>tdog, and the skeleton snatches it out of the air with a butterfly <sound>ne</sound>t.

乳.meaning: A <part>stork</part> flies in with a baby, and the baby's first cry is a <part>zigzag</part> wail across the night sky. The stork knows just what to do: it swoops off and comes back with a warm bottle of <kanji>milk</kanji>.
乳.on: At the café the baby points at the me<sound>nu</sound> and orders a triple, with extra froth.
乳.kun: A <sound>chee</sound>tah and her <sound>chee</sound>tah cub creep up and lap the spilled drops off the floor.

寺.meaning: On a mound of <part>soil</part> at the top of the hill, a monk practises with a <part>golf club</part>, chipping balls quietly between the bells and the incense. One careful swing a day. This is his <kanji>temple</kanji>.
寺.on: He drives up the mountain every morning in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, his clubs rattling in the back.
寺.kun: When a swing goes wrong, the ball bounces off a <sound>te</sound>nnis net, and the other monks cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

質.meaning: A jeweller tests a <part>shellfish</part> pearl by tapping it with two little <part>axe</part> heads. Tap, tap: a fake would crack. This one rings like a bell. It's the real thing, with real <kanji>substance</kanji>.
質.on: She wraps the pearl up in a soft cotton <sound>shee</sound>t so it won't get scratched.
質.kun: She dunks it in a <sound>tu</sound>b of water, and a curious <sound>chee</sound>tah peers in to watch it shine.

問.meaning: A huge <part>mouth</part> sits in the middle of the <part>gate</part> and won't let anyone through until they answer it. 'How many stars are in the sky?' it booms. You scratch your head. Every traveller must answer its <kanji>question</kanji>.
問.on: The mouth belongs to a hairy <sound>mon</sound>ster hiding behind the doors.
問.kun: Stuck, you ask the <sound>to</sound>tem pole beside the gate, but it just stares back at you.

恋.meaning: A <part>jellyfish</part> drifts into the shallows and sees a lifeguard on the beach. Its see-through body glows pink, and its <part>heart</part> thumps so hard you can watch it beat. It's head over tentacles: a summer <kanji>romance</kanji>.
恋.on: A little <sound>wren</sound> carries love notes between them, back and forth over the waves.
恋.kun: In the pond nearby, two <sound>koi</sound> swim nose to nose, blowing heart-shaped bubbles.

園.meaning: A tall fence runs right round the edge like a <part>cage</part>, and inside it a lady in a <part>ball gown</part> strolls between the flowerbeds, feeding the ducks. Swings, a pond, a bandstand: it's the town <kanji>park</kanji>.
園.on: At closing time a tiny train with a puffing <sound>en</sound>gine takes everyone round the paths one last time.
園.kun: Someone has dumped an old <sound>so</sound>fa by the pond, and the park keeper cries '<sound>No</sound>!'

庭.meaning: Out from the <part>shed</part> marches the whole <part>imperial court</part> in a long parade: queen, cooks, guards and goats. Round and round they go on the paving stones, walls closing them in on every side. It's the palace <kanji>courtyard</kanji>.
庭.on: A gardener marks out a new flowerbed in the middle with sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
庭.kun: Weeding between the stones, the gardener bumps his <sound>knee</sound> and cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!'

直.meaning: A drill sergeant stands on a stool shaped like a <part>ten</part>, one stern <part>eye</part> on his recruits. Each must stand by a <part>pole</part> on <part>one</part> painted line. 'Fix that slouch!' he barks, and they all snap upright <kanji>straightaway</kanji>.
直.on: As a reward, each recruit gets a square of <sound>choc</sound>olate, eaten standing to attention.
直.kun: One recruit snaps his <sound>na</sound>an in half, then sticks it back together: '<sound>Oh</sound>, good as new!'

妻.meaning: Every morning a <part>woman</part> hangs her <part>rake</part> on a <part>pole</part> above <part>one</part> long shelf in the shed, right where it belongs. Her husband keeps losing his. She never loses hers. She runs the garden, and she's his <kanji>wife</kanji>.
妻.on: They toast every harvest together with a jug of apple <sound>ci</sound>der.
妻.kun: When he sneezes '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' in the dusty shed, she hands him a <sound>mu</sound>g of hot tea.

関.meaning: An <part>alien</part> lands outside the city <part>gate</part> and knocks. The guards check its papers: it's the mayor's second cousin! Family gets in, so the doors swing open. Turns out everyone here is <kanji>related</kanji>.
関.on: The mayor greets it with a pink <sound>car</sound>nation pinned to one antenna.
関.kun: At the gate, a <sound>se</sound>tter dog runs off and fetches the big iron <sound>key</sound>.

係.meaning: On a <part>coat hook</part> in the hall hangs a long cord of <part>lineage</part>, with one knot for every grandparent, aunt and cousin. Tug any knot and all the others twitch. Each one has a <kanji>connection</kanji> to the rest.
係.on: Tug it at a party and a whole birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke wobbles at the other end.
係.kun: In the family pond a <sound>ca</sound>rp is in charge, another <sound>ca</sound>rp is its deputy, and they both look after a little coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

央.meaning: A <part>large</part> man spreads his arms under a <part>blanket</part> held up like a tent. It drapes down from his head on both sides, and he stands exactly in the middle holding it up. He's the tent pole at the <kanji>center</kanji>.
央.on: Right at the center of the forest stands one huge <sound>oa</sound>k, and every path leads to it.
